label: There is a PLG-consistent set of sequents over the natural numbers from which n + 1 ≺ n is…
paraphrase: There is a PLG-consistent set of sequents over the natural numbers from which n + 1 ≺ n is derivable for every n, so derivable strict partial ground from it is not well-founded. Hence the rules of PLG, Non-Circularity included, exclude cycles of strict ground (for consistent assumptions) without excluding infinite descending chains of strict ground. It is a claim about PLG derivability, not that actual ground descends infinitely.
